## Close record — change 2001 MERGED as `d841921e1d`; all four ACs met

### Three things that belong on this ticket permanently

**1. The size ladder was DEAD CODE, not merely wasteful — this corrects both the parent ticket
and this ticket's own description.** `plan_review/sizing.py` orders its handlers
`except LLMUnavailableError: raise` (`:522`) BEFORE the arm that consults
`is_context_limit_error` (`:524`). Python matches `except` clauses top-to-bottom and
`LLMUnavailableError` IS-A `Exception`, so the ladder could never see the provider signal it was
built for. It did not "burn a full failed round-trip per rung": it burned exactly ONE chunk call
and aborted the whole review to an unsigned INDETERMINATE. Measured against the real
`pass1_with_ladder`, varying only the exception type on identical code — wrapped: 1 call, then
propagate; raw `ModelHTTPError` or any non-`LLMUnavailableError` type carrying the same message:
3 calls, the documented batch -> one-criterion-per-call fallback, and two P8
"reduce/decompose" findings. Resurrecting that fallback is the real argument for the fix; the
saved round-trips are a rounding error beside it.

**2. The attribution was DERIVED, not inherited, and it diverges from the parent's on purpose.**
This is a **regression** from `fuel-posse-ball` (`96fe-14c6-4c35-4936`), commit `4e4d055e0f`
(2026-06-25) — one commit that introduced BOTH the blanket `LLMUnavailableError` wrap and the
`except LLMUnavailableError: raise` guard that hides the ladder from it, two days after the
ladder shipped in `527e856e6e` (2026-06-23). Its own commit message states both halves. That is
a genuine good->bad transition, so `--class=regression`.

The parent ticket (`undamaged-adolescent-sable`) attributed ITS defect to `66b3-4214-c70b-4a9a`
as an omission. I did not carry that over; I re-derived from this mechanism's own history and
reached a different ticket and a different class. Also recorded: a line-scoped
`git blame -w -C -M -L 144,167` on the fix site names `dcc90ced450`, `f2ea9c7e91` and
`c3d5c5c8fa` — all three are CARRIERS (a completion-verifier change and two refactors that moved
the line), and all three FAIL the date test by postdating the 2026-06-25 transition. Walking
through them reaches `4e4d055e0f`. `civilized-immediate-mamba` and `authorial-hated-blackbear`
were considered and rejected: mamba scoped itself to metadata explicitly and named blackbear as
the owner of the wiring, and blackbear's ACs covered exit codes and stderr messages, not the
raised type. Neither created the contradiction.

**3. Mutation M9 SURVIVED and is disclosed rather than buried.** The kill matrix ran 9 seeded
defects across the independent sides of the fix; 8 died. M9 — reverting `gate_dispatch`'s two
mid-run companion arms — survived, and the disclosure is the point: no driver I could build
reaches those arms, because a runner whose `preflight` passes and whose `run` raises is absorbed
into the finders-failed tail before reaching them, with `emit_gate_error` never firing. The
**control is what makes this reportable rather than alarming**: the PRE-EXISTING
`LLMUnavailableError` does not reach those arms either, so this is a standing coverage gap, not
one this change introduced. Filed as `shaggy-crass-bull` (`c72a-48be-054d-4005`),
`discovered_from` this ticket, with the alternative disposition written into it — if the arms are
genuinely unreachable they are dead code and should be deleted, not maintained. The companion
change is kept meanwhile because it can only prevent an escape, never cause one.

Two instrument failures were caught rather than inherited, and both are worth the next reader's
attention. The first kill-matrix run reported **all 9 mutations surviving** — a shell
arg-passing bug meant no patch was ever applied; the tell was the log echoing the description
where the mutation id belonged. The rewritten harness `assert`s that each patch changed the file
before running, keys the verdict on pytest's EXIT CODE rather than grepping colorized output,
and was self-tested against known-broken code first. Separately, M8 initially survived the
ENTIRE pre-existing unit suite, so the oracle was strengthened rather than the result accepted.

### AC ticks — all four met, with one nuance recorded rather than reworded

Ticked (checkbox characters only; no AC prose altered — the edit diff was exactly four
characters with zero length delta).

- **AC#1** — `test_a_change_input_failure_is_not_raised_as_a_provider_outage` (context-400, 413,
  `ContentFilterError`) plus `test_the_providers_own_text_survives_the_rewrap`. Offline
  throughout; no live provider.
- **AC#2** — `test_the_new_type_stays_inside_the_shared_error_vocabulary`.
  **Nuance, recorded here rather than by rewording the AC:** the AC says the subclassing means
  "the 13 existing broad handlers keep catching it", and that is true and verified — every
  `except LLMError` site, including both CLI surfaces, is unaffected. But it does not follow that
  NO handler needed changing: four NARROW `except LLMUnavailableError` handlers stopped catching
  this class and had to be widened to preserve today's behaviour (`epic_bug_screen` x2,
  `gate_dispatch` x2), and the Step-7 parity sweep found a fifth (`container_stage:209`). The AC
  is met as written; its phrasing just under-describes the blast radius, and a reader should not
  infer from the tick that the type swap was containment-free.
- **AC#3** — `test_a_genuine_outage_still_raises_the_outage_type`, 9 parametrized rows (500, 503,
  529, 429, 401, a malformed non-size 400, `ConnectError`, `ReadTimeout`, unknown `RuntimeError`),
  each asserting `type(...) is LLMUnavailableError`. This is the AC that a relabel-everything
  change would fail while still satisfying AC#1 and AC#2, and mutations M2 and M7 confirm it has
  teeth.
- **AC#4** — `test_retry_statuses_are_unchanged` and `test_fallback_eligibility_is_unchanged`.

### Verification

`make lint` clean (complexity ratchet `active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`), `make typecheck`
clean, full unit sweep **12127 passed / 44 skipped**, all re-run on the rebased tree. Change 2001
patchset 2 earned `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` and merged as `d841921e1d`; the merged commit
carries this ticket's trailer and Change-Id `I5cb2a5e9…`, and all ten files are byte-identical to
the reviewed patchset (verified by blob SHA, since Gerrit rebased on submit).
